title: Publish chain: push scenarios → JFRED → jfredToolsPlugin, verify clean-room + marketplace, sync wrapper clone
description:
Consolidated go-public checklist from four implementation-notes files:
(1) User must push the scenarios repo (1 unpushed commit 075ef56 "added S86, updated S41") BEFORE JFRED is pushed — JFRED's pin was fetched from the local clone and dangles for cloners until then.
(2) JFRED is staged but uncommitted; first commit + push still needs the privacy gate re-run at push time. Commit ordering: commit inside jfred/jfredToolsPlugin first, push, then re-stage the gitlink in JFRED (it currently records the license-only commit 70ad1b6), commit JFRED, then RevEng.
(3) Consider switching the GitHub default branch for matkatmusic/jfred from master (empty initial commit — a plain git clone gets an empty tool) to develop: `gh repo edit matkatmusic/jfred --default-branch develop`.
(4) After pushing jfredToolsPlugin to https://github.com/matkatmusic/jfredToolsPlugin, verify the install flow with a real `claude plugin marketplace add matkatmusic/jfredToolsPlugin` + `claude plugin install`, then decide whether the zshrc --plugin-dir wrapper (task 108's interim enablement) should be retired.
(5) ~/Programming/jfredToolsPlugin (the clone the claude() wrapper actually loads) does NOT yet have the two new scenario skills — pull/push the canonical $REVENG/jfred/jfredToolsPlugin changes into it after committing, or /impl-scenario and /plan-scenario won't resolve at the next launch (their RevEng copies are now archived).
(6) Deferred verifications left for the user from task 111: RevEng `npm test` (5 task-workflow tests + 2 python tests remain), `npm run typecheck`, clean-room `npm test`, and the interactive /run-scenario check under `command claude`.

title: Build the task-119 failure-path fixture + launch.json entry, then exercise the missing-rev-card click (t124:Q2)
description:
The task-119 failure UI (health banner, dashed gap rows, coverage strip, placeholder rev-cards) has never been exercised live — no failure fixture exists. Steps:
(1) Copy the sanitized demo bundle jfred/demo/ (s87 session) into a REPO-LOCAL dir (e.g. jfred/demo-corrupt/, not a tmp scratch dir that gets cleaned) — do not touch the original.
(2) In the copied JSONL, find a mid-session Edit on a file with several revisions and mangle its payload so REPLAY fails (e.g. change the edit's old_string so it no longer matches). Do NOT invent an unknown record type — that still crashes the viewer before the consent dialog (known s87 trap); use a valid record whose replay fails.
(3) Add a new configuration to RevEng/.vscode/launch.json — clone the existing "Debug viewer server (port 7343)" entry (program jfred/src/viewer_server.ts, cwd jfred, preLaunchTask build:webapp) but name it "Debug viewer server (failure fixture)" and point --projects-dir at the corrupted-bundle dir.
(4) Load the session, pass consent, open the affected file to see the failure UI; clicking the placeholder rev-card currently shows a carried-forward diff instead of the failure reason — that's the t124:Q2 problem to observe (and the fixture doubles as the failure-path test fixture task 119 never had).

title: jfred: clone-ready .vscode launch.json/tasks.json (demo bundle + ~/.claude/projects)
description: Add .vscode/launch.json + tasks.json INSIDE the jfred repo (not RevEng/.vscode — those don't ship to cloners) so anyone who clones jfred can spin up the viewer server and test the tool in their browser. launch.json needs 2 configurations: (1) launch viewer_server with --projects-dir pointing at the sanitized demo bundle jfred/demo/ (the s87 session, same data as npm run demo); (2) launch viewer_server with --projects-dir pointing at ~/.claude/projects (the user's real sessions). Both should reuse the existing build:webapp preLaunchTask pattern from RevEng/.vscode/launch.json's "Debug viewer server (port 7343)" entry; tasks.json carries that build task. Check jfred/.gitignore doesn't exclude .vscode/.

title: Unrecoverable rev-card: replace the raw engine error with a user-useful message
description: Change the unrecoverable rev-card's message to "L:n (of N) failed to <whatever> [{ }]" — the current message (the raw replay error, e.g. "TypeError: hunk.lines is not iterable") is not providing useful information to the end user, whereas the preferred message does: which line/revision failed, out of how many, and what operation failed to apply. Render site: buildMissingRevisionCard in jfred/webapp/views/details-revision-cards.ts (the .why div carries card.unrecoverableReason verbatim; the reason string originates in unrecoverableRevision, jfred/src/reconstruction_replay.ts). Exercise with the task-126 failure fixture ("Debug viewer server (failure fixture)" launch config, session ee3482f5, inventory.py rev 8).

title: Unrecoverable rev-card: add [Jump to timeline step] and [{ }] buttons
description: The unrecoverable rev-card needs '[Jump to timeline step]' and '[{ }]' buttons so the user can inspect the JSONL line and see where in the timeline the failed reconstruction occurred. Healthy cards get both via buildRevisionActionsElement (jfred/webapp/views/details-revision-cards.ts); buildMissingRevisionCard deliberately omits the whole action row because content/export/patch actions would lie for a carried-forward placeholder — add ONLY these two buttons (the card carries the changeId both need: jumpToOwningTimelineStep + context.openRecordForChangeId). Exercise with the task-126 failure fixture.
